candidates.title: A second comparison of the same runs rewrites the first comparison's title and keeps it in the first maker's name
candidates.area: Proforma Studies: comparisons (POST /api/studies/comparisons, ProformaStudies, ProformaComparison, export)
candidates.statement: When a person compares runs another maker already compared in the same order, the service replaces the kept comparison's title with the new one and keeps the row's by and at as the first maker's, so the first title is lost with no audit row and the new words stand in someone else's name, in the screens and in the export package.
candidates.contract: docs/api/studies.md:127 "the same runs in the same order are one comparison"; CLAUDE.md:56 "Every scientific row carries `project_id`, `created_by` and `created_at`"; CLAUDE.md:8 "every claim, number and result stays inspectable back to its source"
candidates.expected: The one comparison keeps the title its maker gave it (Ada's "A"), or the second ask is refused in words, or it is kept beside it in Ben's name; nothing a maker wrote is replaced without a trace.
candidates.observed: Fresh database: Ada compares corn and sugarcane titled "A: Ada's question"; Ben compares the same two runs titled "B: Ben's question". The service answers and keeps {'id': 'abbdad1a765bffe6', 'title': "B: Ben's question", 'by': 'Ada', 'at': <Ada's time>}; the comparisons table row reads created_by Ada, title B; no audit row names a comparison. On the copy of the development database, comparing e7efa2505b4633de and 784c94d9bd67d20e from Studies as Hunt Fourteen replaced claude-sonnet-5-5's title "Hot-water versus dilute-acid pretreatment, integrated bioprocess, package defaults: uncertainty review" with mine; the comparison page then said "2 runs set side by side for claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-08 02:38 UTC" under my title, and the export package's study.json carried my title with by claude-sonnet-5-5.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/studies/comparisons.py:266-273 (make: the id is the artifact's, content-addressed; `held` keeps by and at, the title is the asker's; `_put` calls rows.put, core/openferment_core/db/rows.py:59-66, an upsert that replaces the body)
candidates.evidence: Ran repro_comparison_title.sh on bh_h14_cmp (port 8943): the second POST answered title B by Ada, GET listed one row title B by Ada, psql showed created_by Ada with body title B, GET /api/audit held no comparison row. In the browser (scripts/full4.mjs on bh_h14_full) the comparison page showed my title for claude-sonnet-5-5; shots/full4-comparison.png; export unzipped under the scratch export folder.

candidates.title: A kept strain's aliases never resolve a record's organism: every strain page and Hosts card counts no record
candidates.area: geneOS Hosts and strain pages, Catalogues, anchoring (validate.strain_id), fermOS strain binding
candidates.statement: Anchoring resolves a paper's organism wording through validate.vocabulary(), whose strain map is always empty in the service, so no record ever names a kept strain's id, and every strain page, the Hosts coverage counts and fermOS's strain filter find no record for any strain, while the tests that claim the resolution patch a vocabulary in.
candidates.contract: docs/api/intake.md:94 "`aliases`, the other names papers give it" and intake.md:106 "The readers that had read an empty list read these: geneOS's hosts and the strain aliases"; src/screens/Organisms.tsx:46-47 "anchoring resolves the wording a paper uses to a strain's id by the name and the other names its entry keeps (validate.strain_id on the service)"; core/openferment_core/validate.py:1165-1167 "the organism, resolved to a strain id where the wording names one (an exact alias, or an alias standing in it as a whole word)"
candidates.expected: With a strain kept under the alias "Ethanol Red" (and the paper's full wording), a candidate whose organism is "Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ethanol Red" is anchored with organism = the strain id and organismText = the wording, and the strain page lists it.
candidates.observed: The candidate is kept with organism "Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ethanol Red", organismText None, strainId None; catalogues.as_strain_aliases() holds {'ethanol red': 'ethanol-red', 'saccharomyces cerevisiae ethanol red': 'ethanol-red'} while validate.vocabulary()['strains'] is {} and strain_id(...) is None. In the browser on the copy, a strain kept with alias "Ethanol Red" shows "0 papers 0 records ... No record in this project carries an organism tag naming Ethanol Red (H14)" while 22 records name "Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ethanol Red"; GET /api/fermos/bind?family=batch_v1&sugar=glucose&strain=h14-ethanol-red binds no growth record.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/validate.py:874-891 (vocabulary() with no path returns strains = {}; nothing reads catalogues.as_strain_aliases, core/openferment_core/catalogues.py:600, except module_stores); readers match the anchoring-time id: src/screens/StrainPage.tsx:564-568, src/screens/Organisms.tsx:49-50, core/openferment_core/fermos.py:1507-1514. Hollow tests: core/tests/test_validate.py:160-169 and core/tests/test_fermos_bind.py:139-142 monkeypatch validate.vocabulary with a strain table the service never builds (2 passed here)
candidates.evidence: repro_strain_alias.sh on bh_h14_alias (port 8942): candidate through POST /api/tools/biorepo_write?by=... (anchoring, no model), overlay row {'organism': 'Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ethanol Red', 'organismText': None, 'strainId': None}; Python in the service's venv printed the catalogue's aliases beside an empty anchoring vocabulary. Browser: scripts/full8.mjs, shots/full8-strain.png and full8-geneos.png. pytest tests/test_validate.py -k 'resolves or alias': 2 passed.

candidates.title: BioRepo Search's Answer with no key says "ModelUnavailable: generation failed (see server logs)" and names no key
candidates.statement: With no key, the answer stream's error hides the service's own words ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set ...") behind the kit's generic "generation failed (see server logs)", where the route promises the stream says there is no key; the stream also carries four event kinds the contract leaves out.
candidates.contract: core/openferment_core/api.py:2146-2150 (and docs/api/openapi.json for the route) "One model call through llm.py, under the day's cap; with no key the stream says so in an `error`"; the 200 response's description "Server-sent events: `delta`, `citations`, `done`, or `error`"
candidates.expected: event: error with words naming the missing key (the words Intake's Extract toast and Postdoc show: "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set. Put it in core/.env ...").
candidates.observed: event: error data {"code": "generation_failed", "message": "ModelUnavailable: generation failed (see server logs)"}; the service log holds detail='ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set. Put it in core/.env (gitignored) and restart the service.'; the screen shows "ModelUnavailable: generation failed (see server logs) The service log says why." The stream also sends retrieval_started, retrieval_done, compression_done and generation_started.
candidates.cause: core/.venv/.../sci_rag/answer/generator.py:300-311 replaces any exception's text with its class name; core/openferment_core/literature/kit.py:805-841 passes the kit's error event through, and openFerment's own ModelUnavailable words (llm.py) never reach it
candidates.evidence: curl -N POST /api/literature/answer on bh_h14_full and on a fresh bh_h14_scr (repro_screens.sh): the error event above, the log line above; browser scripts/full1.mjs, shots/full1-answer-nokey.png. No request left the machine: llm.py refuses before any call.

candidates.title: The bench files a decimal comma as a number ten times larger: "7,4 g/L" is kept as 74 g/L
candidates.statement: The capture box strips every comma before reading a number, so a reading said with a decimal comma ("titre came in at 7,4 g/L") is filed as a measurement of 74 g/L, where the matcher's own rule is to keep a doubtful line as words.
candidates.contract: src/engine/capture.ts:8-12 "matching is deliberately conservative: when in doubt this returns null and the text is kept verbatim as an Observation ... a false positive silently writes a number into a slot it does not belong in"
candidates.expected: "7,4 g/L" kept as an observation (a comma between digits with one or two after it is doubtful), or filed as 7.4.
candidates.observed: "titre came in at 7,4 g/L" -> {value: 74, unit: "g/L"}; "1,250 g/L" -> 1250. The read-back beat shows "74 g/L, you said 7,4 g/L", the one guard before a scenario may take the reading as a measurement.
candidates.cause: src/engine/capture.ts:25-31 (normalise removes every comma before the number regex at :100)
candidates.evidence: Ran capture_comma.ts against the tree's capture.ts with tsx; the bench in Chromium filed "20,500 kg/hr" as 20500 (scripts/full6.mjs), the path that holds a thousands comma right.
